data.content_ref: inline:The preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on Popper's terms as a non-inductive rational choice: we select the theory that has withstood the most severe tests not because we expect it to remain true (which would be induction), but because it is currently the best-criticized and least refuted option available. This survives as the stronger case, but the cost is accepting that science offers no assurance of future success or probability of truth, only a commitment to the most rigorously tested error-elimination strategy at hand.
